pr_body:
The TLS protocol mismatch message during handshake in older JDK 8 is different. 

This is a fallout from https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/67337

Closes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/67511

issue_context.title: [CI] [7.x] SSLDriverTests.testHandshakeFailureBecauseProtocolMismatch failures
issue_context.body:
<!--

**Build scan**:
https://gradle-enterprise.elastic.co/s/oagxtkhqkf3jy
https://gradle-enterprise.elastic.co/s/7akgi2ktv5ot4

**Repro line**:
```
./gradlew ':x-pack:plugin:security:test' --tests "org.elasticsearch.xpack.security.transport.nio.SSLDriverTests.testHandshakeFailureBecauseProtocolMismatch" -Dtests.seed=E397264D250D880B -Dtests.security.manager=true -Dtests.locale=sr-CS -Dtests.timezone=America/St_Kitts -Druntime.java=8
```
**Reproduces locally?**: Yes

**Applicable branches**: 7.x

**Failure history**:
https://build-stats.elastic.co/goto/30a7ec831d753f0b753e6c60af3fa5ff

**Failure excerpt**:

```
org.elasticsearch.xpack.security.transport.nio.SSLDriverTests > testHandshakeFailureBecauseProtocolMismatch FAILED
    java.lang.AssertionError:
    Expected: is "The client supported protocol versions [TLSv1.1] are not accepted by server preferences [TLS12]"
         but: was "Client requested protocol TLSv1.1 not enabled or not supported"
        at __randomizedtesting.SeedInfo.seed([E397264D250D880B:7F0274DCF1FD49A3]:0)
        at org.hamcrest.MatcherAssert.assertThat(MatcherAssert.java:18)
        at org.junit.Assert.assertThat(Assert.java:956)
        at org.junit.Assert.assertThat(Assert.java:923)
        at org.elasticsearch.xpack.security.transport.nio.SSLDriverTests.testHandshakeFailureBecauseProtocolMismatch(SSLDriverTests.java:189)
```

Failure relates to #67324
comments: @albertzaharovits do you mind taking a look since this looks similar to #67324 ?

@jkakavas This is my bad.
In #67337 I've dropped the assert for the older TLS mismatch error message, which is still emitted on JDKs 1.8 that are still packaged by some linux distros.

Another failure which contains the fix but still fails. Can you check @albertzaharovits ?

https://gradle-enterprise.elastic.co/s/wlg73jwpaspd6

The reason is that `org.bouncycastle.tls.TlsFatalAlert: protocol_version(70)` is thrown only by BCJSSE which is used with JDK >=11 or with Azul Zulu 8. So when the above runs with JDK 8 ( adoptopenjdk, corretto, oracle ), the CI is using SunJSSE which throws 
```
anyOf(is("The client supported protocol versions [TLSv1.1] are not accepted by server preferences " +
                    "[TLS12]"), is("Client requested protocol TLSv1.1 not enabled or not supported"));
```
@jkakavas Thanks for the pointer. Is there a configuration for that? Can you help me figure out how did you figure it out?

> Is there a configuration for that?

Yes, see : 
https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/7.x/gradle/fips.gradle#L17 and https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/61857

We don't expose that back somehow, so there's no property like `BuildParams.runtimeJavaDetails` that can be used in the test. One could iterate the list of providers and their names to determine if SunJSSE or BCJSSE is used but I don't think it's worth it. I'd suggest we add the matcher for the BCJSEE error in the `anyOf`

> Can you help me figure out how did you figure it out?

Well, the " org.bouncycastle.tls.TlsFatalAlert: protocol_version(70) is thrown only by BCJSSE" comes from painful memories :) and that was actually the hint. `org.bouncycastle.tls.*` sounds like it comes from the JSSE (BCJSSE vs SunJSSE ) provider and not the crypto (BCFIPS) provider if you think about it. ( the `tls` part ) .

Aaarg, only in the 7.x branch, I could've peered into the master branch all day. Makes sense to sit in 7.x only, but I was fixated on master.
Thank you!

I'll use the anyOf trick.

> Aaarg, only in the 7.x branch

Yeap, its a Java 8 only thing. After Java 9, SunJSSE dropped support for FIPS 140-2 mode so we only use BCJSSE ;)
